Thanks for the report, and for the minimal example.

There are two separate things going on here:

1. **Why `dummy_method` disappears from `getmembers(type(obj), ismethod)`:** `inspect.ismethod` only matches bound methods. When you pass the class, `dummy_method` is a plain function, so it is not a bound method. Using `inspect.isfunction` on the class should list it:

   ```python
   methods = getmembers(DummyBaseModel, isfunction)
   ```

   Passing the instance to `ismethod` works because the methods are bound at that point.

2. **The deprecation warning with `getmembers(obj, ismethod)`:** `getmembers` walks `dir(obj)` and calls `getattr` on every name. That reaches the deprecated `__fields__` attribute on the instance, which triggers `PydanticDeprecatedSince20`. Since this is triggered by ordinary introspection rather than by your code, it may be worth a closer look on our side. Using `getmembers(type(obj), isfunction)` as above avoids the instance access in the meantime.

If that doesn't match what you need, let us know what you're trying to collect and we can look at it further.

The root cause analysis (Apple's `ld_prime` reserving less Mach-O header padding, and Homebrew's `install_name_tool` step needing it) is clear, and the link to the related cryptography discussion is helpful. A maintainer will take a look at the build-side change. Thanks for your patience.

Thanks for the detailed request! Treating empty (or whitespace-only) strings as unset and falling back to a default is a reasonable use case, especially with pydantic-settings. We'll take a look at how it fits with the existing `env_ignore_empty` setting and per-field options like `StringConstraints`. We don't have a timeline to share yet, but we appreciate you flagging it.

Thanks for opening this, and for the detailed follow-up from the discussion.

You're right that `warn_untyped_fields` isn't listed in the docs' "all strictness flags" example, even though the heading suggests it should be. We're looking into whether the docs should cover it, and whether the plugin should validate unknown `[tool.pydantic-mypy]` keys, since unrecognized keys are currently ignored silently.

We haven't made any decisions on timing yet. Thanks for helping keep the docs accurate.

Thanks for the report, and for the detailed traceback! The failure happens while `pydantic_core` is being imported, in `typing_extensions`' use of `getattr(typing, name)` under Python 3.15.0a8 with `-X lazy_imports=all`. That makes it look like an interaction with the new lazy-import behaviour in the alpha rather than something in your code. We haven't confirmed the root cause yet. It would help to know whether the same error occurs with a newer 3.15 alpha or beta, and whether it also happens with `-X lazy_imports=all` in a fresh environment that only installs `pydantic` and `typing_extensions`. Thanks again for trying out the upcoming Python release.

Thanks for opening this, and for the detailed checklist! Adding Pyodide/PyEmscripten wheel build support tracks the PEP 783 work and the related PR (#13157). We've noted the open items: the maturin release with pyemscripten support, the CI changes to drop the Rust nightly requirement, and the documentation updates. No timeline to share yet, but we appreciate the progress here.

Thanks for the report, and for the clear reproduction and suggested fix!

You're right that the `None` checks in the `check_passwords_match` example are misleading. Since `password1` and `password2` are typed as non-Optional `str` fields, Pydantic's field validation rejects `None` before the "after" model validator runs, so those branches can't be reached. A cleaner example (with an optional comment explaining this) would avoid suggesting otherwise. Thanks for flagging it; a documentation fix would be welcome.

Thanks for the report and the minimal example! As described, enabling the `pydantic.mypy` plugin appears to hide the `arg-type` error for the keyword argument passed to the model constructor, while mypy without the plugin reports it. A maintainer will take a look. Thanks for your patience.

Thanks for the detailed report and the bisect across versions, that makes it much easier to follow. The minimal example and mypy config are helpful. We'll take a look at whether the `AliasChoices` typing change in 2.11 is causing the `explicit-any` error under `disallow_any_explicit`. We don't have a timeline yet, but we'll update this issue as we learn more.

Thanks for tracking this! This issue is a checklist for Python 3.15 support. Several items are already done (the `MISSING` sentinel update, lazy imports, `TypeForm` usage, and the `base64` changes), and others are linked to open PRs. The remaining open items are the `frozendict` follow-up (waiting on the PyO3 0.30 bump) and the frame pointers investigation. We'll keep this list updated as work progresses.

Thanks for the suggestion, and for offering to help! Keeping AI-generated code current with the latest Pydantic APIs is a real problem. We haven't decided on a SKILL.md (or similar agent-focused docs) for the repo yet, so this is an open question for the maintainers. We'll take a look at it as part of triage. If you'd like to contribute, it would help to share a draft or a short proposal of what the file would cover (for example, v2-only patterns like `model_dump` and `Annotated` in place of v1 idioms). Thanks again!

Thanks for the detailed report and the minimal reproduction! I can see the behaviour you describe: with `polymorphic_serialization=True` set on the model, values inside `dict[str, InstanceOf[BaseModel] | None]` serialize as `{}` by default, while passing `polymorphic_serialization=True` to `model_dump()` gives the expected output. A maintainer will take a look at whether the config setting is being propagated to the dict values as the documentation describes. Thanks for your patience.

Thanks for the report! This looks identical to #13167, which was opened a minute earlier with the same content, so I'm marking this one as a duplicate of that issue. Please follow along there.

One thing to check: the error shown here is an `openai.BadRequestError` raised from the OpenAI client path in autogen (`OpenAIChatCompletionClient` with a Gemini model), and there's no Pydantic traceback or `model_validator` code in the reproduction. If you believe Pydantic is involved, could you share a minimal, self-contained example that uses only Pydantic and shows the `mode='wrap'` validator receiving a raw dict? That would help us tell whether this is a Pydantic issue or one for the autogen/OpenAI-compatibility side.

Thanks for the report, and for the clear explanation of the annotation on `BaseModel.__class_getitem__`. We've added it to our triage queue. In the meantime, using `NoneType` (from `types`) as the type argument, as you suggested, should avoid the type checker complaint. We can't promise a timeline, but we appreciate you flagging it.

Thanks for the detailed report and reproducer! It's clear how `create_generic_submodel` drops `__slots__` from the origin when building parameterized classes, which explains the `__weakref__` reappearing on `Model[X]`. We've added this to our triage queue for maintainer review. Thanks for also sharing the workaround.

Thanks for the detailed request, and for linking the earlier discussion (#2980) and the related issue (#9537).

This looks like a feature request for a global config option that makes enums serialize and deserialize by member name instead of value, with JSON schema reflecting names. I've tagged it as a feature request so the maintainers can review it. We can't promise if or when it will be picked up, but the context you've provided is useful.

Thanks for the detailed report! I was able to follow both examples.

The second part (`model_copy(update=...)` accepting unknown fields when `extra="forbid"` is set) looks like the same behaviour reported in #7581, which is closed. A maintainer will take a look at how this should be handled.

The first part (`model_copy(update=...)` with a private attribute name ending up in `__dict__` rather than replacing the private value) looks like a separate problem, so it may need its own tracking. Thanks again for flagging both.

Thanks for the detailed report and the fuzzing find! You're right that `fraction_validator` only catches `ValueError`, so a zero denominator like `"6/0"` escapes as a raw `ZeroDivisionError` rather than a `ValidationError`. Adding `ZeroDivisionError` to the caught exceptions, as you suggested, looks like the right direction, and a regression test for `"6/0"` would be a good addition. Thanks for taking the time to narrow this down.

Thanks for the detailed write-up, and for linking #10409. The gap you describe is real: `TypeAdapter` gives you the right flat shape for a top-level discriminated union, but not the model-style API (`model_validate`, direct field access), and `RootModel` adds a `.root` layer. This looks like a feature request, and we've tagged it that way so maintainers can weigh it against other priorities. We can't commit to a timeline, but the use case and the trade-offs you laid out are useful input.

Thanks for the detailed report and the clear before/after reproduction. The change in behaviour between 2.12.5 and 2.13.4 is useful to have pinned down. We'll take a look at why `StrEnum` keys passed to `create_model` are no longer normalised to plain `str` field names.

Thanks for the report and the minimal reproducer! The example makes it easy to see the problem: `super()` inside a `slots=True` dataclass subclass fails on Python 3.13.7 but works on 3.14. We'll take a look at reproducing it and confirming the cause across Python versions. Thanks for your patience.

Thanks for the report! This looks like a duplicate of #11358. When an earlier field fails validation (here, the missing required `price`), Pydantic still calls the `default_factory` that takes the data dict, and that dict doesn't contain `price`, so the factory's `data["price"]` raises a `KeyError` instead of the `ValidationError` for `price` being surfaced. Following that issue for the underlying fix. In the meantime, your workarounds (a default for `price`, or checking for the key inside the factory) should avoid the error. Thanks for the detailed example!

Thanks for the detailed report and the minimal reproduction, @MaxG87. The version table and the stack trace are very helpful.

You're right that a segfault shouldn't happen here, even though the model in the example is ill-formed. We've labeled this as a V2 bug so a maintainer can take a closer look at how the PEP 695 alias recursion is handled during `model_rebuild()`.

We didn't find an earlier issue that reports this same crash, so we're leaving it open. Thanks again for reporting it.

Thanks for the report, and for the minimal reproducer! Nested `|` and `&` compositions in `pydantic.experimental.pipeline` crashing with an internal `AttributeError` during schema generation is not the behavior we want, whether composition should work or give a clear error. We've marked this as a bug and will take a look. Thanks also for offering to contribute; contributions are welcome, and the contributing guide covers how to get started.

Thanks for the detailed report and the reproducer! The output shows that with `@validate_call`, the `dict` and `list` arguments the function receives are new objects rather than the ones the caller passed in, so mutating them inside the function doesn't affect the caller's originals. The `BaseModel` instance keeps its identity in your example, which is consistent with how model instances are passed through validation. A maintainer will take a look to confirm whether this is the expected behavior for validated containers or something to change. Thanks for your patience!

Thanks for the detailed report, and for linking the MariaDB Connector async dialect source. You're right that `MariaDBDsn` currently rejects `mariadb+mariadbconnector_async://...` because the underlying URL parser doesn't accept underscores in the scheme. A maintainer will take a look and let you know how it fits with the existing URL types. Thanks for your patience.

Thanks for the detailed report, and for the clear reproduction and explanation of the test interaction with `pytest.warns`.

From the example, when `@computed_field(deprecated=...)` wraps a property that is itself decorated with `@deprecated(...)`, the warning emitted is the inner `@deprecated` message rather than the `computed_field` one. We'll take a look at how the two deprecation messages are resolved. Thanks again for filing this so it can be tracked.

Thanks for the detailed report and the minimal example! You've correctly identified the asymmetry: `pathlib.WindowsPath` isn't handled in the same place as `pathlib.PosixPath`, so `Path("config.toml")` as a default produces different JSON schema output on Windows and Unix. We'll look into it and confirm the expected behavior for `WindowsPath` defaults. Thanks for taking the time to narrow it down.

Thanks for the clear report and minimal reproduction! As described, the `Annotated` metadata on the generic parameter appears to be dropped in 2.13 when the model is parametrized with `Annotated[...]`, and wrapping it in `Optional` avoids the problem.

We've tagged this for generics and annotations so a maintainer can take a look. I can't give a timeline. Also, the versions in your report read as pydantic 2.12.5 and 2.13.4 (not 3.x), so we've assumed that's what you meant.

Thanks for the detailed write-up, @deuxcents. The FastMCP use case of searching with partially filled models is clear.

This looks like a feature request for a new `Prototype` annotation, so I've labeled it as such. A maintainer will review it when they can. Feel free to add any further thoughts on the proposed API, or on how `model_construct` should handle dictionaries for `BaseModel` fields (#8084), in the meantime.

Thanks for the detailed report and minimal reproduction! You're right that the annotation on `__pydantic_extra__` (`Dict[str, T]`) isn't used when generating the JSON schema for `DictAlike[Model1]`, so the `additionalProperties` ends up as `{}` and the `Model1` definition is missing, while the plain `Dict[str, T2]` field works as expected. We've added this to our triage queue to look into. We can't promise a timeline, but we appreciate you taking the time to write this up.
